_readme: This file is the whole site. Edit it, run 'python build.py', refresh. Text fields support **bold**, *italic*, [link](https://…) and newlines.

site.description: Joyal Joy Madeckal and Anjana Raju invite you to their ring exchange and their wedding. Details and RSVP.

invitation.lead: Two celebrations, two months apart — and we would love you at both.
invitation.body: PLACEHOLDER — two or three sentences here. Where you met, or simply that you're glad they're coming. Keep it short; the details are below.

functions.name: Ring Exchange
functions.tagline: A small evening with family and close friends.

functions.name: The Wedding
functions.tagline: The ceremony, then dinner and dancing until late.
functions.note: Ceremony and reception are at the same venue, so there's no travel in between.

details.title: Good to know
details.intro: The same for both events unless noted.

items.description: PLACEHOLDER — see the label on each event above. The wedding reception is on grass, so heels will sink.
PLACEHOLDER — parking, nearest station, shuttle times.
PLACEHOLDER — a hotel or two near the wedding venue, plus any block-booking code.
PLACEHOLDER — say plainly whether kids are invited, and whether that differs between the two events.
PLACEHOLDER — registry link, or a sentence saying your presence is enough.
PLACEHOLDER — e.g. phones away during the ceremony, then share everything after.

rsvp.title: Will you join us?
rsvp.intro: Reply for each event separately — you're welcome at one or both. Please let us know by **PLACEHOLDER DATE**. One form per household is fine.
rsvp.note: We'll email you a confirmation. Change of plans? Just reply to that email.

labels.name: Your name
labels.song: A song that will get you dancing

messages.sent: Thank you — we've got your reply.
messages.failed: That didn't send. Please email us instead and we'll add you by hand.
